title: Implement impact-weighted burn windows and tiered paging to cut alert noise
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Following the 2026-02-28 capacity regression that caused a multi-hour token latency SLO breach across hosted inference, we need a combined mitigation and prevention effort to reduce noisy burn-rate paging and prioritize pages by real customer impact. This ticket drives design and implementation of an impact-weighted burn-rate calculator, tier-aware page thresholds, and a short-term automated quiet-window to prevent cascaded alert storms during capacity events. Goals: 1) Reduce actionable pager volume by 60% without materially increasing time-to-detect real incidents; 2) Ensure burn alerts correlate with estimated customer cost/latency exposure rather than raw percentile spikes; 3) Ship safety hards that stop paging during known incident escalations and avoid churn from transient load spikes.
acceptance_criteria: New burn-rate alert computes a weighted score that factors request volume, customer tier, and error/latency impact
Pagering only triggers for weighted score above threshold and sustained for a hysteresis window (configurable)
On-call runbooks updated to reflect new thresholds and escalation flow
Dashboards show before/after pager count and median detection time; targeted reduction >= 60% in non-actionable pages over 30 days
Automated quiet-window mechanism implemented and tested that prevents duplicate paging for bursty, self-healing regressions
tasks: Design weighted-burn formula and run experiments on past 90 days of telemetry
Prototype backend computation in alerting-service with feature flags
Implement per-customer-tier thresholds and hysteresis in alert rules
Add 'incident context' tag to burn alerts so runbooks can surface likely causal capacity changes
Create UI controls in Console for operators to tune quiet-window and thresholds
Add unit and integration tests; end-to-end smoke test in staging
Prepare runbook and update oncall rotation guidance
Rollout via canary in two stages: non-critical region, then all regions
notes: Rationale: Current burn-rate pages fire on percentile shifts that produce many noisy pages during transient spike events (e.g., autoscaling jitter, short GC storms). Engineering analysis of the Feb incident shows ~72% of pages had negligible customer impact (low-volume tenants or internal traffic). Weighting by estimated affected customer minutes and median latency delta should better prioritize truly impactful events. We will keep a low-level aggregate signal for metrics/alerts but avoid immediate paging unless the weighted score passes threshold.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): offline scoring design + run historical scoring over telemetry and pick thresholds. Phase 2 (week 3-4): implement feature-flagged alerting-service changes, add hysteresis and quiet-window. Phase 3 (week 5): UI controls and runbook updates, staged canary rollout. Phase 4 (week 6-8): measure and iterate; if target reductions are not met, tune weight factors and expand suppression rules.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression could delay detection of genuine incidents -> Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, dual-channel notification (ESM and slack) for low-weight alerts
Risk: Weight model complexity causes runtime overhead in alerting pipeline -> Mitigation: pre-aggregate weights at 30s buckets and memoize customer-tier lookups
Risk: Operators confused by new metrics -> Mitigation: training doc, tabletop exercise during rollout
monitoring_signals: Total pager count (by SLO type) pre/post rollout
False-suppression incidents (cases where suppression prevented legitimate pager)
Customer-visible latency and error rate by tier
comments: 2026-03-05 — Aisha Kaur: Created ticket after postmortem review. Initial scoring proposal attached (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PLAT-401).

2026-03-07 — Liam Chen: Ran historical scoring over 90 days; initial thresholds would have suppressed ~58% of pages with <5min customer impact. Added as artifact (s3://redwood/analysis/weighted-burn-90d.csv).

2026-03-09 — Priya Menon (SRE): Reviewed design. Requested hysteresis window >= 3m and a hard cap that forces paging for any incident touching enterprise-tier customers. Also suggested a 'soft-alert' Slack channel for low-weight events.

2026-03-11 — Design review (Marta Lopez): Console control should include a live preview that shows expected weekly page reduction at current settings. Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/alert-hysteresis-v1.pdf.
2026-03-12 — Security (Jamal Ortiz): No security concerns; scoring uses only metadata and aggregated telemetry. Recommended ACL audit for who can change thresholds.

2026-03-13 — Liam Chen: Implemented prototype in feature-flag branch; unit tests green. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/4123. Performance microbenchmarks show alert evaluation latency increased by ~12% at worst, acceptable.
2026-03-14 — Aisha Kaur: Updated acceptance criteria and scheduled canary for 2026-03-21. Please add any dependencies or objections before EOD 2026-03-16.
